belief: Real men don't cry or ask for help.
origins: Boys hear “Man up” and “Stop crying” from family, coaches, and peers. They learn to hide fear, sadness, and need, and later struggle to ask for help even when they are hurting. Many men carry pain silently for years.
teaches: “Jesus wept.” David, a warrior king, wrote, “I am weary from groaning; all night I flood my bed with weeping.” Paul, a hardened apostle, said, “I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest on me… For when I am weak, then I am strong.” “Two are better than one… if one falls down, his companion can lift him up.” The strongest Man who ever lived wept, asked His friends to stay with Him, and received help carrying His cross. Strength includes honesty and humility.
self_statements: Asking for help means I am less of a man.
I have to be the rock.
I cannot let anyone see me struggle.
errors: Believing a man is either strong or weak.
Feeling vulnerable and concluding it is unsafe.
Predicting that I will be dismissed.
questions: Who taught me that real men do not cry or ask for help?
What did Jesus, David, and Paul do?
What does silence cost me and the people I love?
Which men do I respect, and are they really emotionless?
Who could I trust with something real?
What is one small step I could take?
truth: Strength includes honesty. Jesus wept, David wept, and Paul embraced weakness. I can feel, speak, and ask for help, and that makes me a better husband, father, friend, and follower of Christ.
hw_truths: David poured out his tears to God.
When I am weak, then I am strong.
log: Each week, note one time you named a feeling or asked for help.
actions: Write who taught you and what they said.
prayer: Lord, I learned to hide what I feel. Teach me the strength of honesty and the humility to ask for help. Amen.
name_example: Tom can write: “Jesus wept, and I can be honest too.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Real men don't cry or ask for help.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
